first_reader_check.about: Whether passing a tagged released mathematics item requires the tagged competency, tested without student data by searching for assessment bypasses: solvers that lack the competency by an explicit restriction on their operations or their information, never see the key, and pass under the published scoring rule.
first_reader_check.shown: Under a pre-registered bar, language models of two families recover New York Regents Algebra I and Algebra II keys with every given quantity withheld, and the recovery survives a change of every option value with the form kept; on those items a pass does not require computing on the givens, and whether it requires the tagged operation is left open. Small programs denied the tagged operation match keys on a few cells. TIMSS cognitive-domain cells yield no bypass at their public sizes. Claimed rates are measured on items re-read from the printed page, which released text layers often misstate.
first_reader_check.what_is_new: The assessment bypass as a one-sided, student-free test of a tag, with two restriction kinds (capability and information) that are the same object; a pre-registered witness bar with hashed programs and Holm correction inside each solver family; a census of 2,405 tagged public-release items; and the measurement finding that the released text layer must be replaced by a page re-read before any rate is claimed.
first_reader_check.why_a_big_deal: Accountability, curriculum evaluation, and research read a tagged pass as evidence of the tagged competency. Where a solver denied the given quantities matches the key on both Regents algebra cells, on every scorer, and with every option value changed, the key does not carry the evidence it is read as on those items. The abstract states that consequence in one clause: so the key does not carry the evidence it is read as.
abstract_says: first paragraph: the tag, the reading, the assumption the reading makes, the bypass as the test (glossed inline), one-sided in one sentence

second paragraph: pre-registered bar; Algebra I and II language-model bypass in two model families surviving the option-value change; the consequence for the key as evidence; the tagged-operation question left open; small programs on a few cells; TIMSS null at public sizes; claimed rates measured on the printed page
few numbers: none in the abstract beyond the two cell names and the two model families
first_reader_check.no_conjunction_contradicted_by_a_table: The abstract conjoins Algebra I and II recovery with survival under the option-value change; Table tab:isomorph shows every scorer clearing on both cells under the rank-preserving arm on the repaired-verified population.
first_reader_check.intro_lead: A released mathematics item carries a published tag ... A correct answer is then read as evidence of the tagged competency ... That reading assumes that passing requires the competency. The second paragraph names the bypass, its one-sidedness, and where the requirement question sits relative to alignment tools and psychometrics; the third paragraph states what was found; four contribution bullets of one or two sentences follow. The formal notation (S, C, T, R) and the claim-ladder table are gone; the ladder is one sentence in words.

circular_definition.note: assessment bypass is glossed inline in the abstract and in intro paragraph 2, and defined once in Method 3.1

first_reader_check.body_first_reader: Method defines bypass, restriction kinds, items, families, bar and Holm families, controls, print fidelity, and the two codings once each in that order. Results run measurement layer, language-model bypass with isomorph and codings, capability-restricted rows, TIMSS null and controls. Related Work keeps the collective-advance paragraph and states the object in one clause. Limitations state each limitation once and no result twice.
